people.role: Founder (970) and head of Dạ Quang Môn; the desert raider who knelt to Băng Tâm in 1121
people.appearance: A huge grey-bearded rider with a burn across one side of his face and a jade cup that glows on his belt at night.
people.backstory: Hạng Dạ Bôi was born in 870 into the Hạng, a caravan-guard family of Trường Vân Thành (A120), and rode the Pavilion's caravan road for eighty years. In 968 a caravan of Băng Tâm's tax silver was lost to the sand, and the Desert Pavilion hanged his elder brother for it. Two years later Hạng took the guards the Pavilion had dismissed and became the thing they had guarded against: Dạ Quang Môn, bound to no lord (C172). For a century and a half his raiders drank grape wine from night-glowing cups after every raid and left one cup behind as their mark (A121). In 1119 Băng Tâm marched (C184). In 1121 it burned Huyết Đao Trại, where his loot was hidden and his first wife Lâu Minh Châu (lau_minh_chau) died (V074). He knelt to Sở Ngọc Hồ (so_ngoc_ho) and gave her his son Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa) as surety (C185). Since then his raiders have guarded the caravans they used to rob (A123). He is 330, and he has not forgiven anything. When his young blades began drinking from the cups again (A126), he poured the first one himself.
people.wants: His son home before he dies, and one day to watch the Keeper of the Vessel kneel.
people.secret: The Pavilion burned the wrong fort. Dạ Quang's real hoard lies under the sand at Mai Sa Bảo, buried in 1050 (V073): enough stones to hire a war.

people.role: Hạng Dạ Bôi's second wife and first blade; voice of the raiders who would break the knee
people.appearance: A lean desert woman in red felt, with a hawk feather knotted to her sabre and a smile that the Pavilion's envoys do not like.
people.backstory: Đồ Xích Linh grew up in the felt tents of Chiên Trướng Thôn and rode with Dạ Quang from the age of sixteen. By 1100 she led its fastest band. In the Taming (C184) she killed more Băng Tâm riders than anyone, and took the sabre of one of them, a hawk feather still on its hilt. She did not kneel in 1121; she was not asked, because the Pavilion did not know her name. She married Hạng Dạ Bôi (hang_da_boi) four years later, after Lâu Minh Châu (lau_minh_chau) burned, and gave him a daughter, Hạng Lưu Hỏa (hang_luu_hoa). She has never met Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa), and she prefers it that way. To her the knee was a pause, not an end. She has been writing to the ma đạo cultivator Triệu Huyết Y (trieu_huyet_y), who knows blood arts deeper than the Canon. She pays in stones from her own gambling.
people.wants: Her daughter named heir, and Dạ Quang unbound from the Pavilion within her husband's lifetime or after it.
people.secret: She is learning a blood art from Triệu Huyết Y, and she would let Băng Tâm keep the hostage forever if it clears her daughter's road.

people.role: Hạng Dạ Bôi's daughter; leader of the young blades who drink from the cups again
people.appearance: Her father's height and her mother's smile, in a riding coat with a night-glow cup sewn on the breast.
people.backstory: Born after the knee, she has never raided. She has only heard about it. In 1194 she was the first to drink from the night-glowing cups again (A126), and half the young blades of Dạ Quang now follow her. Her mother Đồ Xích Linh (do_xich_linh) wants her named heir. She is not sure she wants her half-brother Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa) to stay a hostage. She has never met him and writes to him every year.

people.role: Captain of Dạ Quang's caravan escorts since 1121
people.appearance: A weathered, tidy rider from the camel-bell town who keeps the escort's ledgers in a hand better than his master's.
people.backstory: He rode in the raids as a young man and was made escort captain when the raiders were set to guarding the caravans they had robbed (A123). To everyone's surprise he is good at it, and likes being paid. Trấn Sa Đường's watcher Nhiếp Cô Đăng (nhiep_co_dang) follows every escort he rides. He is the one Dạ Quang man the merchants of Hồi Lan Thành trust.

people.backstory: A Hồi Lan Thành merchant's daughter taken in a raid in 1080 who chose to stay, married Hạng Dạ Bôi (hang_da_boi), and kept Dạ Quang's books for forty years. She bore Hạng Minh Sa (hang_minh_sa) in 1100. In 1121 she stayed in Huyết Đao Trại to burn the ledgers before the Pavilion could read them, and burned with them (V074). Because of her, the Pavilion never learned of Mai Sa Bảo.
